findings.issue: applyHumanRiskReview enforces the known-severity check over ALL record.facts, but `labels` can only contain the sampled case ids (riskLabels.length === cases.length plus dup and full-case-coverage checks above). For any fact whose severe was pre-frozen by main (typeof fact.severe === 'boolean') and whose id is NOT among the sampled cases, labels.get(fact.id) is undefined !== fact.severe, so import always throws assistant_quality_known_risk_changed. Schemas explicitly permit facts (max 10000) to be a superset of the sampled cases (>=100), and hasFrozenRiskCoverage/exportedRiskFacts confirm facts are keyed as a superset of cases — so any population where main pre-labels severity on non-sampled facts makes the human risk-review stage permanently un-importable (fail-closed dead end, but it defeats the designed 'pre-frozen-main-or-human' stage and blocks qualification until code change).
findings.minimalFix: Restrict the non-downgrade loop to facts that are part of the review: `for (const fact of record.facts) { const l = labels.get(fact.id); if (l === undefined) continue; if (fact.severe === true && l !== true) throw Error('assistant_quality_known_risk_changed'); }` — i.e., skip non-sampled facts and enforce non-downgrade (true must stay true) rather than strict equality, so a human upgrade false→true is not falsely rejected.

findings.issue: hasFrozenRiskCoverage revalidates a stored riskReview (assessmentId, label count/dups, labels match current severe) but never checks review.data.digest === record.digest, unlike applyHumanRiskReview which enforces digest at import. A record upserted with changed facts/cases (new digest) but identical severe flags would still pass coverage with a stale risk review attested against different frozen facts, weakening the attestation-to-frozen-facts binding.
findings.minimalFix: Add `review.data.digest !== record.digest` to the rejection conditions in hasFrozenRiskCoverage.

findings.issue: Deterministic sampling sorts sha256 hex digests with localeCompare, whose ordering is ICU/locale-dependent; cross-environment (or ICU-upgrade) runs could theoretically produce a different sample for the same frozen dataset, breaking the deterministic-sampling contract. For pure ASCII hex, code-unit comparison is the correct stable order.

limitations: Static review only; no tests, commands, or file reads executed; no live config, credentials, or source data supplied.

Main native export/import and the full workflow (generation captured before native await, post-await context/model/record revalidation under SAVEPOINT, phase transitions, reimport_id consumption) are separate reviewed scope and were not assessed; their approval is not implied here.

Reachability of the P1 depends on the omitted population() port returning pre-labeled facts beyond the sampled case ids; the presented schemas and hasFrozenRiskCoverage's superset lookup explicitly permit that shape, and nothing in scope forbids it.

Whether the workflow stores applied labels inside record.dataset.cases affects reimport behavior (exportedQualityFacts would then include labels and mismatch a previously exported `frozen` block); this could not be verified from the scoped files.

readQualityRecord() picks the latest assessment by rowid, which ON CONFLICT upserts do not advance; correctness of 'latest record' selection under the omitted workflow's write pattern could not be verified.
